provenance: Recorded via `RECORD_INVERSE_WORK=1 pnpm run record:inverse-work` (P0.109). Never hand-edit: inverse-solve-work.test.ts re-measures every row live and asserts deep equality, so an edited number lands red rather than passing. UNLIKE inverse-solve-perf.json, NOTHING HERE IS MACHINE-SPECIFIC. Given the same code and the same `tolerance`, these counts are identical on any machine -- asserted directly by inverse-solve-perf.test.ts's determinism case -- which is why this is a separate artifact rather than a block inside the timing one. It also means a change to these numbers is always a change to the code or the tolerance, never to the hardware, and should be explained as such. `stepsPerEval`, `meanStepMs`, `rejectedPerAccepted` and `rhsPerStep` are derived from the four raw counts and the time of flight; they are stored rather than recomputed so that a reader sees the same numbers the assertions use.

attribution._summary: P0.109 asked which of three suspects -- step count, rhs cost, or stiffness -- explains why these three targets cost 10-100x the library median. THE ANSWER IS WORK VOLUME, AND THE RIGHT UNIT IS THE RHS EVALUATION, NOT THE ACCEPTED STEP. Dividing inverse-solve-perf.json's recorded medians by this file's nRHS gives 0.676-0.848 us across all 18 integrating targets -- a spread of 1.25x, against the ~3600x spread in cost per solve. A solve costs its rhs evaluations times a constant, and nothing else. THE UNIT IS NOT A PEDANTIC POINT: per ACCEPTED STEP the same division spreads 2.3x, because a rejected step pays its stages and then contributes nothing to the divisor. frozen-ou-gust is the whole of that discrepancy and is ordinary once measured per rhs. RHS COST PER EVALUATION IS THEREFORE RULED OUT as a differentiator -- every target pays the same -- and so is A HARDER SOLVE: all three converge in as few Newton iterations as the fast targets (the filing already said so; it is asserted here so a regression cannot quietly change it). BUT THE THREE DO NOT SHARE A REASON FOR THEIR RHS COUNT, AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING: one flies far longer, one takes far smaller steps, and one throws nearly half its work away. Reading them as a single 'slow scenarios' bucket would be wrong. Each is described below. ONE CAVEAT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the timing artifact records frozen-ou-gust converging in 3 Newton iterations and this run measures 2; every other target agrees exactly. That row therefore divides a 3-iteration time by a 2-iteration count, which OVERSTATES its us/rhs -- and it still lands mid-pack, so the conclusion survives the discrepancy rather than resting on it.
attribution.density-altitude-2000m: FLIGHT DURATION. IRREDUCIBLE -- it is the scenario. It is launched at y0 = 2000 m and falls the whole way, so it flies 73.6 s against a library median near 3 s and 3.4x the next-longest target (cannonball-muzzle, 21.4 s). Its steps are among the LARGEST in the library and its rejection rate is the LOWEST, so the controller is not struggling: there is simply more trajectory to integrate. Nothing can be reduced here without changing what the scenario is, and the scenario's whole point (blueprint density-altitude exhibit) is the long carry.
attribution.dust-grain: STIFFNESS. IRREDUCIBLE WITH AN EXPLICIT STEPPER. The shortest mean step in the library, over a flight SHORTER than the library median -- so the step count comes from step size, not from duration, which is the opposite of density-altitude-2000m. The steps are small AND ACCEPTED (rejection rate 0.021, ordinary), which is the signature of stiffness rather than of a controller overshooting: the error estimate is satisfied by a step this small because the physical relaxation time is this short. At micron scale the Stokes relaxation time is orders below the flight time, and SCENARIO_LIBRARY's own note already calls this entry 'genuinely stiff' -- this measures what that note asserts. dopri5 is an explicit non-stiff method, so its step is bounded by stability, not accuracy, and no tuning of it helps. An implicit or IMEX stepper would; that is a solver-kit capability this repo does not have and is not part of this task.
attribution.frozen-ou-gust: STEP REJECTION, and it is different in kind from the other two -- this is the one with headroom. It rejects 0.84 steps per accepted step against a library median near 0.07, more than 4x the worst of anything else (lofted-mortar, 0.19). That is visible in the rhs count rather than inferred: a rejected dopri5 step still pays its stages, so this target spends 11.9 rhs per accepted step against ~6.4 for the library -- i.e. ROUGHLY 46% OF ITS INTEGRATION WORK IS DISCARDED. It has the LARGEST nRHS in the library (176614) despite flying for 4.4 s, a fifth of cannonball-muzzle's flight. The cause is the scenario's frozen Ornstein-Uhlenbeck gust path: sampled once into a fixed realisation, it is continuous but rough, and an embedded error estimator that assumes a smooth solution repeatedly proposes steps the roughness then rejects. NOT REDUCED HERE. A fix means changing the gust field's interpolation or the controller's response to it, both of which reach outside this harness and need their own measurement; filed as P0.151. Note what the headroom is NOT: eliminating every rejection would remove ~46% of this target's rhs work, which is worth having and is still not close to the 10-100x the filing is about. This target would remain slow.
